Biplot-region surrogate model

bl_surrogate.Rd

Assigns each observation's predicted class using the nearest contour line in Z-space rather than the fitted classifier. The surrogate provides a purely spatial approximation of the decision boundary confined to the training-data hull.

Usage

bl_surrogate(bl_result, data = NULL)

Arguments

bl_result

A "bl_result" object from bl_assemble().

data

Data frame to classify. Defaults to bl_result$train_data. Must contain all columns in var_names.

Value

A list of class "bl_surrogate" with components:

surrogate_pred

Integer vector; surrogate class per obs (0 or 1).

model_pred

Integer vector; model-predicted class per obs.

class_obs

Integer vector; true labels (NA if absent in data).

accuracy_vs_model

Numeric; agreement rate with model predictions (computed over in-hull observations only).

accuracy_vs_labels

Numeric; accuracy vs true labels (NA if no labels available; in-hull only).

n_total

Integer; total number of observations scored.

n_in_hull

Integer; observations inside the training-data polygon.

hull_coverage

Numeric in [0, 1]; fraction of observations inside the polygon. Accuracy metrics are computed only over in-hull observations.

boundary_set_nr

Integer vector; contour index assigned per obs.

z_boundary_type

Numeric vector; probability level per retained contour.

Z_obs

n x 2 matrix; Z-space coordinates of each observation.

bl_result

Reference to the parent bl_result.

How the surrogate works

The surrogate uses ct_surrogate contour lines always computed and stored in bl_result$biplot_grid$ct_surrogate by bl_build_grid(). These contours are generated with cells outside the training-data convex hull set to cutoff before extraction, so all contour lines are fully enclosed within the hull.

Each observation is first projected to Z-space. Observations that fall outside the training-data convex hull polygon are excluded from the surrogate classification — they receive surrogate_pred = NA — because the surrogate regions are defined only within the hull. A message reports how many observations were excluded. Accuracy is computed on in-hull observations only.

In-hull observations are assigned to the nearest contour segment in Z-space. The contour's probability level determines the surrogate class: level < cutoff → class 0; level >= cutoff → class 1.

Accuracy is reported against (in-hull observations only):

  • The fitted model's predictions (accuracy_vs_model)

  • True class labels when present in data (accuracy_vs_labels)
